NaRoomData__Meta.NaRoomData__UnitNote: Floor areas in square metres, measured wall to wall inside the room. 1 m² = 10.7639 ft².
NaRoomData__Meta.NaRoomData__SourceSheet: Room size sheet (Google Sheets), pasted 16-Nov-2026. Sheet log: 18-Jul-2023, bedroom with fitted wardrobes added.
NaRoomData__Meta.NaRoomData__Method: Each room was checked against published UK standards, surveys and trade guidance, using non-UK sources only where no UK source exists. Values were changed only where a UK standard sets a higher floor (the Nationally Described Space Standard for bedrooms, Approved Document M for wheelchair-accessible bathrooms) or where the room is sized by equipment that several makers document (sauna cabins, cue tables, cinema seating rows, and greenhouses and conservatories sold in set sizes). Elsewhere the sheet's values stand, with notes where the sources point higher or lower. The sheet's own values are kept beside every change.

NaRoomData__EvidenceScale.High: Several independent sources agree, including a UK standard or several UK makers.
NaRoomData__EvidenceScale.Medium: Four or more sources broadly agree, mostly trade or design guidance.
NaRoomData__EvidenceScale.Low: Fewer than four usable sources, or only indirect evidence. Values kept as supplied unless a standard applies.

NaRoomData__Cleaning: Blank rows, empty columns and the Updates footer removed. The Bedroom Suite and Granny Annex headings became groups, and every other room was placed in one of eleven groups.
Units were not stated in the sheet; the figures are square metres (a 9 ft² living room is impossible). Every room was checked to rise strictly from Min to O/S.

Four pairs of duplicate rows merged under the UK name, the other kept as an alias: Walk-in Closet into Walk-in Wardrobe, Mudroom into Boot Room, Study/Office and Home Office into Study / Home Office, Home Theater into Home Cinema.
Spelling and naming: Granny Annex to Granny Annexe, equiptment to equipment, Home Theater to Home Cinema, Game Room to Games Room, Sunroom to Sunroom / Conservatory.
Atrium had no figures in the sheet and none could be sourced, so it is listed but left out of the comparisons.

NaRoomData__Rooms.NaRoom__Notes: The LABC Warranty survey of 10,000 listed homes puts today's new-build living room at 17.1 m², down from 24.9 m² in the 1970s; Medium 20 m² matches homes built up to the 2000s. London's design standards want the main sitting space at least 3 m wide (3.5 m for three or more bedspaces), so 9 m² (3 × 3 m) is the floor. Open-plan kitchen, living and dining spaces are larger: London's combined minimum is 23 m² for a 1-bed 2-person home and 27 m² for a 2-bed 4-person home.

NaRoomData__Rooms.NaRoom__Notes: Added to the sheet on 18-Jul-2023. The NDSS counts a built-in wardrobe inside the bedroom's floor area (as long as it does not narrow the room below the minimum widths), so the floor for any bedroom is still 7.5 m²: Min raised from 6. Fitted wardrobes are about 600 mm deep and need 600–900 mm clear in front, the same as freestanding ones, so the sources give no general reason for a smaller room. The sheet's 1 m² saving on the other bands holds where the wardrobes fill alcoves that would otherwise be wasted: treat it as a design judgement.
